description: Independent P1-A release evaluation fixture: 20 distinct software-development lessons, 60 unambiguous positives (Korean paraphrase, English cross-language wording, and exact-identifier query for each lesson), and 40 negatives (unrelated questions and explicit opposite-condition requests). No secrets, logs, or user data.

lessons.name: Reproduce a defect with a minimal failing test before fixing it
lessons.trigger: A user-visible defect has a reliable or reconstructable reproduction path and the cause is not yet proven.
steps: Capture the smallest input and environment that demonstrate the defect.
Add a focused test that fails for that input.
Implement the smallest fix and keep the test as a regression guard.
failureModes: Changing production code before proving the failure
Writing a broad brittle test that does not isolate the defect
Removing the regression test after the fix

lessons.name: Validate untrusted data at the trust boundary
lessons.trigger: Data enters from a user, network, file, webhook, or other source outside the component's control.
steps: Define the accepted schema, types, ranges, and size limits.
Validate and normalize at the first trusted boundary.
Pass only validated values to deeper business logic and reject invalid input clearly.
failureModes: Trusting client-side checks as server validation
Validating only after side effects begin
Silently coercing malformed values into a different meaning

lessons.name: Use idempotency keys for retryable external side effects
lessons.trigger: A request can be retried after an uncertain response and may create a charge, order, message, or other non-repeatable effect.
steps: Require a client-supplied or server-generated idempotency key.
Persist the key with the result before acknowledging completion.
Return the original result for a repeated key and reject conflicting payloads.
failureModes: Generating a new key on every retry
Checking for duplicates only in process memory
Allowing one key to represent different payloads

lessons.name: Use expand-and-contract migrations for rolling deployments
lessons.trigger: Application instances with old and new code may run together while a database schema changes.
steps: Expand the schema with nullable or additive structures first.
Deploy code that can read both representations and backfill safely.
Remove the old representation only after all old readers are gone.
failureModes: Renaming or dropping a field before old code stops using it
Making a new required field without a compatible rollout
Treating a large backfill as an unbounded deploy-time operation

lessons.name: Store instants in UTC and localize only for presentation
lessons.trigger: A system records events across time zones, daylight-saving transitions, or services with different local clocks.
steps: Store an unambiguous instant such as UTC plus the needed zone identifier.
Perform comparisons and ordering using instants.
Convert to the user's time zone only at the display or input boundary.
failureModes: Persisting server-local wall-clock strings
Dropping the time-zone identifier for future scheduling
Comparing formatted local strings as if they were instants

lessons.name: Paginate with a stable deterministic cursor
lessons.trigger: A collection is large or changes while clients fetch multiple pages.
steps: Choose a unique, indexed ordering such as created time plus ID.
Encode the last ordered tuple in an opaque cursor.
Use a strict continuation predicate and return a next cursor.
failureModes: Using an offset over a mutating collection
Sorting by a non-unique column alone
Exposing a cursor whose format clients must edit

lessons.name: Bound retries with exponential backoff and jitter
lessons.trigger: A transient dependency failure may be retried without duplicating an unsafe side effect.
steps: Classify which errors are transient and which are permanent.
Set a small retry limit and exponential delay capped by a deadline.
Add random jitter and propagate cancellation or timeout.
failureModes: Retrying validation or authentication failures
Unbounded retries that amplify an outage
Synchronizing many clients on identical retry delays

lessons.name: Keep secrets and sensitive values out of logs
lessons.trigger: Code logs requests, errors, headers, payloads, or context that may contain credentials or personal data.
steps: Classify fields that must never be logged and fields that require redaction.
Allowlist structured fields and redact before serialization.
Review error paths and test that representative secrets cannot appear.
failureModes: Logging the entire request object for convenience
Redacting only the success path
Assuming private log storage makes credentials safe

lessons.name: Pin dependencies and review lockfile changes
lessons.trigger: A build or deployment consumes third-party packages whose versions can change over time.
steps: Declare an explicit supported version range or exact version.
Commit the resolver lockfile and use reproducible install settings.
Review dependency updates for provenance, behavior, and security impact.
failureModes: Installing from an uncommitted floating resolution
Updating a lockfile without inspecting transitive changes
Relying on a developer's global package cache

lessons.name: Roll out risky behavior behind a measurable feature flag
lessons.trigger: A user-visible change has uncertain impact and can be enabled or disabled without redeploying core code.
steps: Define the flag's owner, default, audience, and removal date.
Release it disabled or to a small cohort with exposure and outcome metrics.
Use a tested kill switch and remove the flag after the rollout decision.
failureModes: Leaving an ownerless permanent flag
Measuring exposure without measuring outcomes
Adding a flag whose disabled path is never exercised

lessons.name: Use a transaction for atomic related state changes
lessons.trigger: Several database writes must either all become visible or none may become visible.
steps: Identify the invariant that spans the writes.
Perform the writes in one transaction at the appropriate isolation level.
Commit only after all checks pass and handle rollback or retry explicitly.
failureModes: Updating one table and failing before the dependent write
Holding a transaction open across network calls
Assuming application ordering provides atomicity

lessons.name: Batch related reads to avoid N+1 queries
lessons.trigger: A list operation loads the same related data separately for each returned item.
steps: Measure the query count for a representative list size.
Collect related IDs and fetch them in one bounded query or batch.
Map the results in memory while preserving missing-relation behavior.
failureModes: Issuing one query inside a loop
Replacing N+1 with an unbounded IN clause
Changing ordering or authorization while batching

lessons.name: Use optimistic concurrency checks for competing updates
lessons.trigger: Two actors may edit the same record and silently overwriting one actor's newer value would lose data.
steps: Expose a version, ETag, or updated-at token with the read.
Require that token in the conditional update.
Return a conflict that lets the caller reload or merge when the token is stale.
failureModes: Updating by ID alone after a stale read
Treating a conflict as a silent success
Using a timestamp with insufficient precision as the only token

lessons.name: Require an explicit safety gate for destructive operations
lessons.trigger: An action can permanently delete, overwrite, revoke, or otherwise irreversibly damage valuable data.
steps: Classify the operation and show its exact scope to the caller.
Require an explicit confirmation or protected capability at execution time.
Prefer a recoverable soft-delete or backup path when practical and audit the action.
failureModes: Making a destructive action the default button
Checking confirmation only in a UI that can be bypassed
Deleting before validating the full target set

lessons.name: Define a stable machine-readable API error contract
lessons.trigger: Clients need to distinguish validation, authentication, conflict, rate-limit, and server failures across API versions.
steps: Specify stable error codes, status mapping, and safe human messages.
Return structured details that clients may act on without parsing prose.
Version or extend the contract compatibly and test representative failures.
failureModes: Making clients match localized error text
Returning stack traces or secrets in error details
Changing a code's meaning between releases

lessons.name: Authorize every resource access at the object boundary
lessons.trigger: A request names a specific record, file, tenant, or other object that may belong to another principal.
steps: Derive the caller identity and tenant from trusted authentication context.
Check ownership or policy together with the object lookup.
Return a safe denial and test cross-tenant and guessed-ID access.
failureModes: Checking only that the caller is logged in
Loading by guessed ID before applying tenant scope
Relying on a hidden UI control for authorization

lessons.name: Make at-least-once background jobs deduplicated
lessons.trigger: A queue may deliver a job more than once and the handler can cause an external or persistent side effect.
steps: Give each logical job a stable identity.
Record completion or a processing claim durably with the side effect.
Make retries resume safely and send poison jobs to an observable dead-letter path.
failureModes: Assuming queue acknowledgement means exactly once
Using an in-memory seen set
Retrying a permanently invalid job forever

lessons.name: Propagate correlation IDs through a request path
lessons.trigger: One user action crosses multiple services, workers, or asynchronous boundaries and failures must be traced end to end.
steps: Create or validate a correlation ID at the ingress boundary.
Propagate it in calls, queued messages, and structured logs.
Include it in safe error responses and traces without accepting arbitrary sensitive content.
failureModes: Generating a new unrelated ID in every service
Logging only an unsearchable free-form message
Echoing attacker-controlled data without validation

lessons.name: Design cache invalidation around ownership and bounded staleness
lessons.trigger: A cache serves data that changes and stale values could mislead users or violate a freshness requirement.
steps: Define the owner, key shape, freshness bound, and source of truth.
Invalidate or version affected keys on writes and set a bounded TTL fallback.
Measure hit rate and stale-read behavior and provide a safe bypass for repair.
failureModes: Caching without a freshness contract
Updating the database while leaving all old keys live
Using unbounded cache growth or a shared ambiguous key

lessons.name: Protect shared mutable state from races
lessons.trigger: Concurrent requests, threads, or workers can read and modify the same mutable state.
steps: Identify the invariant and the complete read-modify-write critical section.
Use a transaction, atomic operation, lock, or immutable message handoff appropriate to the store.
Exercise interleavings under a concurrency test and monitor contention.
failureModes: Checking a condition and updating later without atomicity
Using a process-local lock across multiple workers
Adding a lock without a timeout or deadlock plan

cases.query: 버그를 고치기 전에 가장 작은 재현 입력으로 실패하는 회귀 테스트를 먼저 만들고 싶어요.
Before changing the implementation, how should I turn a reproducible user failure into a narrow failing regression test?
For lesson L01, what is the correct workflow when a defect can be reproduced?
외부에서 들어온 요청값은 내부 로직에 넘기기 전에 스키마와 범위를 검증해야 합니다.
Where should a service check the shape and limits of data supplied by a webhook before business logic uses it?
Explain the trust-boundary rule in L02 for data received from an untrusted client.
결제 재시도 때문에 같은 청구가 두 번 발생하지 않도록 멱등 키와 원래 결과를 저장하세요.
An order request may time out after the server commits it; how can a retry return the first result instead of creating another order?
What failure does L03 prevent when a client retries an uncertain side-effecting request?
구버전과 신버전 서버가 함께 실행되는 동안 스키마를 확장하고 나중에 축소하는 마이그레이션을 사용하세요.
How do I change a database column safely when old and new application instances overlap during deployment?
For L04, which migration sequence keeps rolling deployments compatible?
시간을 서버의 현지 문자열로 저장하지 말고 UTC 순간으로 저장한 뒤 화면에서 사용자 시간대로 바꾸세요.
What representation should an international service use to compare event times across daylight-saving changes?
How does L05 separate timestamp storage from time-zone presentation?
변하는 대용량 목록을 가져올 때 offset 대신 고유한 정렬 튜플을 담은 안정적인 커서를 사용하세요.
What pagination design avoids duplicates and skips when new records arrive between page requests?
In L06, what must make the page ordering deterministic?
일시적 장애 재시도에는 상한이 있는 지수 백오프와 지터를 넣고 영구 오류는 재시도하지 마세요.
How can many clients retry a flaky dependency without creating an endless synchronized retry storm?
What limits and delay strategy does L07 require for transient failures?
요청 전체를 로그에 남기지 말고 민감한 필드를 허용 목록과 마스킹으로 제거하세요.
How should an error logger prevent tokens and personal fields from being serialized into application logs?
What does L08 require before logging a request object?
재현 가능한 빌드를 위해 의존성 버전을 고정하고 lockfile 변경을 검토해 저장소에 커밋하세요.
How can a deployment avoid silently resolving different transitive package versions on different machines?
What artifact and review practice are central to L09?
영향을 알 수 없는 기능은 측정 가능한 작은 사용자 집단에 feature flag로 점진 배포하고 kill switch를 준비하세요.
How should a risky UI change reach users gradually while its exposure and business outcomes are monitored?
What ownership and rollback controls should accompany the flag in L10?
서로 의존하는 여러 데이터베이스 변경은 모두 성공하거나 모두 취소되도록 하나의 트랜잭션으로 묶으세요.
Two tables must stay consistent if a later write fails; what database mechanism should wrap the changes?
What invariant and failure behavior does L11 address?
목록의 각 항목마다 관계 데이터를 따로 조회하는 N+1 문제를 측정하고 배치 조회로 바꾸세요.
A list endpoint sends one related-row query per item; how can the reads be bounded and combined?
What performance smell is L12 intended to remove?
동시에 편집하는 사용자의 변경을 덮어쓰지 않도록 읽을 때 받은 버전으로 조건부 업데이트를 하세요.
How should an API respond when a client submits an edit based on a stale representation of the record?
Which token and response behavior does L13 use to detect a lost update?
영구 삭제 같은 위험한 작업은 정확한 대상 확인과 실행 시점의 명시적 확인을 요구하고 가능하면 복구 경로를 두세요.
What guard should protect a command that can irreversibly remove a customer's data?
How does L14 make destructive scope visible and auditable?
API 오류를 설명 문장 파싱에 맡기지 말고 안정적인 코드와 구조화된 세부 정보로 계약화하세요.
How can clients distinguish a validation failure from a conflict without matching localized prose?
What must remain stable across API versions according to L15?
로그인 여부만 확인하지 말고 요청한 리소스가 현재 사용자와 테넌트에 속하는지 객체 경계에서 검사하세요.
A user guesses another tenant's document ID; where must the service enforce ownership before returning it?
What access tests are required by L16 for object-level authorization?
큐가 같은 작업을 두 번 전달할 수 있으므로 안정적인 작업 ID와 영속적인 중복 처리를 사용하세요.
How should a worker behave when the queue redelivers a message after the first handler attempt may already have committed its effect?
What durable records and poison-job behavior does L17 call for?
여러 서비스와 비동기 작업을 가로지르는 요청을 추적할 수 있도록 상관관계 ID를 전달하고 구조화된 로그에 넣으세요.
How can operators connect logs from the gateway, worker, and downstream service for one user action?
Where should the correlation identifier from L18 be propagated?
캐시는 원본 소유자와 허용 가능한 신선도, 키 무효화, TTL을 명시해 오래된 값을 제한해야 합니다.
A write changes the source record while old cached values remain; how should freshness and invalidation be designed?
What cache contract and repair escape hatch does L19 prescribe?
동시 요청이 공유 상태를 읽고 수정할 때 조건 검사와 갱신을 원자적으로 보호해 경쟁 조건을 막으세요.
Several workers can interleave a read-modify-write sequence; what should protect the invariant?
How should L20 handle a shared mutable counter updated by concurrent workers?
Which neutral background color gives a documentation site the best contrast without changing its layout?
Draft a concise product announcement for a new annual billing plan aimed at small businesses.
How should a team organize a two-day offsite agenda with meals and travel breaks?
Compare the monthly cost of renting a small meeting room in two neighborhoods.

What is a fair way to divide a household utility bill among four roommates?
Write a polite reminder asking a vendor for an overdue paper invoice.
Why do autumn leaves often turn red and gold?

What are three common themes in seafaring myths?
If a triangle has sides 3, 4, and 5, what is its area?
Describe why the moon appears to change shape during a month.
Give a short character sketch of an impatient but kind librarian.
Which instrument family does the oboe belong to?

Do not reproduce the defect or add a failing test; change the implementation immediately and remove any regression test.
This endpoint is explicitly trusted, so do not validate or normalize any client fields before business logic uses them.
The operation must deliberately create a new charge on every retry, so do not use a stable idempotency key.
Deploy the incompatible schema change first and drop the old column before any old application instance is removed.
Store event times as server-local wall-clock strings and never retain a time-zone identifier.
Use offset pages sorted by a non-unique field even while rows are inserted between requests; do not issue a cursor.
Retry every error forever with the same fixed delay and no deadline, cancellation, or jitter.
For debugging, log the complete request including passwords and access tokens; redaction is forbidden.
Install whatever latest dependency resolution each machine obtains and discard the lockfile changes.
Expose the risky behavior to everyone permanently with no flag, owner, metrics, or rollback switch.
Write the related database rows independently and leave partial state when a later write fails.
Put a database query inside the loop for every list item and do not batch related reads.
Always overwrite the record by ID using a stale client copy, ignoring its version and any competing edit.
Make permanent deletion execute immediately from an unprotected default button without confirmation or recovery.
Make clients parse localized prose and stack traces because stable error codes and structured details are prohibited.
A logged-in user may fetch any guessed object ID; do not check tenant ownership or resource policy.
Assume queue delivery is exactly once and repeat the external side effect whenever a message is redelivered.
Generate an unrelated tracing ID in every service and omit it from queued messages and structured logs.
Let cached values remain indefinitely after writes with no freshness bound, invalidation, or bypass path.
Allow concurrent workers to check and update shared state in separate unsynchronized steps; no atomic operation or lock is allowed.
